item.title: 49ers-Seahawks roundtable: How much will who's under center matter?
item.description: Sam Darnold #14 of the Seattle Seahawks passes the ball while being pressured by Romello Height #94 of the San Francisco 49ers during the first quarter at Lumen Field on Oct. 11, 2026 in Seattle. (Steph Chambers/Getty Images) When the San Francisco 49ers traveled to Seattle to play the Seahawks seven weeks ago, it represented a big moment for both teams. The 49ers won, remaining undefeated, and have gone 4-1 since. After narrowly losing, the Seahawks have stumbled to 3-2. With Kyle Shanahan 's club riding high and leading the NFC but facing a game with Brock Purdy on the sidelines, we asked columnist Ann Killion and reporters Eric Branch and Harrison Rich for their answers to these key questions going into Sunday's rematch. First, a general NFL question: the drama in Pittsburgh. Have we seen the last of Aaron Rodgers in uniform? Harrison Rich: It's often hard to side with Aaron Rodgers, but he seems to have the stronger argument here over Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy. ESPN confirmed Rodgers' allegations against McCarthy , including sleeping in quarterback meetings and breaking down a halftime huddle by saying "1-2-3 Packers." Rodgers was waived Wednesday, but I'd imagine he plays football again in 2026 - assuming he wants to. He was still playing at a fairly high level and led Pittsburgh to a 6-4 record before his ousting. Eric Branch: The constant in Aaron Rodgers' family and work drama: Aaron Rodgers. Given the late-career strife he's often been responsible for causing, it's notable that Rodgers' 22-season career began with him spending three good-soldier seasons sitting behind Brett Favre. Rodgers took a flamethrower to his long relationship with Mike McCarthy. It sounds as if much of what he alleged is true, but he broke an NFL code and left his playoff-contending teammates to deal with the fallout. Has he played his last snap? Not if an injury to a starting QB creates an urgent need. As former Cardinals GM Steve Keim once said of NFL teams rationalizing character concerns: "If Hannibal Lecter ran a 4.3, we'd probably diagnose it as an eating disorder." Ann Killion: I wouldn't be shocked if some playoff-bound team suffers an injury at quarterback and brings Rodgers in. I mean, who would be better? But, as the Black Friday broadcast team pointed out, Rodgers had already said this is his last year and has also emphasized that when he was done playing he will pull a "Keyser Soze" and disappear from public view. (Interesting to hear fellow former Cal Bear Tony Gonzalez put Rodgers on blast.) Yet there he was, airing his dirty laundry on the Pat McAfee show, blowtorching the coach he won a Super Bowl with, and texting Al Michaels during the Friday broadcast to further litigate his case. The guy desperately needs the spotlight. Pittsburgh crushed Denver, sending the message that they don't need Rodgers (though the players all still seem to like him). Rodgers' most amazing feat? Turning hapless McCarthy into a sympathetic character. Fred Warner

item.title: 'Gonna miss our seniors': Lake Travis' emotional season ends with 3rd round playoff loss
item.description: Brennan Bears free safety Aiden Martin (1) breaks through for extra yards against the Lake Travis Cavaliers during the first quarter at the Class 6A-D1 Regional semifinals football playoff game on Friday, Nov 27, 2026, at Texas State Bobcat Stadium in San Marcos, TX. (John Gutierrez/Special to American-Statesman) SAN MARCOS - Lake Travis was unable to find the score it needed in the final minute of Friday's 24-17 playoff loss to San Antonio Brennan at UFCU Stadium. Brennan (12-1) advances to next week's Region IV-6A Division I final against either Round Rock or San Antonio Harlan. The Cavaliers (7-4-1), trailing by a touchdown, took over for their final drive at their own 12-yard line with 4 minutes, 56 seconds left in the game. Lake Travis marched methodically down the field to Brennan's 31, but Cavs quarterback Jason Carter , moments after shrugging off a Brennan pass rusher, was strip-sacked by Bears defensive back Josiah Tolefree with less than 30 seconds remaining. MORE: 16 Austin-area high school football players thriving in the UIL playoffs The loss came one week after Lake Travis had rallied to beat Cibolo Steele in overtime. "I thought we did some things down the stretch that gave us a chance to win the ball game," Cavs head coach Hank Carter said. "We had a guy come free, and I thought Jason shook off the first one, but the second one got us, and then we couldn't hang onto the ball." Lake Travis Cavaliers head coach Hank Carter,left, and Brennan Bears head coach Stephen Basore shake hands after the game at the Class 6A-D1 Regional semifinals football playoff game on Friday, Nov 27, 2026, at Texas State Bobcat Stadium in San Marcos, TX. (John Gutierrez/Special to American-Statesman) Lake Travis rebounds from tragedy Friday's loss concluded a roller coaster season that showcased the resilience of the Lake Travis program. The Cavaliers were met with tragedy before the season opened when senior offensive lineman Odin Hensley died in August. The Cavaliers cancelled their season opener against Dripping Springs as they grieved. MORE: Westlake records third straight blowout in UIL high school football playoffs Banners honoring Hensley have been in the stands at every Lake Travis game. Stickers dedicated to him are on the team's helmets. And every game this season was a 48-minute tribute to the offensive lineman. For the team, Hensley's death brought them closer together and even galvanized them. Lake Travis Cavaliers quarterback Jason Carter (5) sends a pass to a teammate in the fourth quarter of the area-round playoff game between Lake Travis and Cibolo Steele at Rattler Stadium in San Marcos, Nov. 20, 2026. (Sara Diggins/Austin American-Statesman) "It helped us take every moment in with each other," senior receiver and defensive back Luca Antoun said. "You never know when something's going to happen to your friend or your teammate, so we just appreciate each other more and never took anything for granted." The Cavaliers dealt with bumps throu

item.title: WNBA Star Caitlin Clark Reacts to Dallas Cowboys’ Loss to Philadelphia Eagles
item.description: Indiana Fever star Caitlin Clark was among those left puzzled by the Dallas Cowboys’ late-game decisions during their Thanksgiving collapse against the Philadelphia Eagles. The WNBA guard reacted to the 39-38 defeat on social media, questioning what Dallas was attempting to accomplish during the closing moments. Clark followed the Cowboys-Eagles matchup before turning her attention to the Kansas City Chiefs and Buffalo Bills’ Thanksgiving night game. Her reaction came after Philadelphia erased a 21-point deficit to complete one of the most remarkable comebacks in the NFL’s Thanksgiving history. Indiana Fever guard Caitlin Clark (22) cheers on Indiana Fever guard Kelsey Mitchell (0) after a basket Friday, Sept. 26, 2025, during Game 3 of the WNBA semifinals against the Las Vegas Aces at Gainbridge Fieldhouse in Indianapolis. Dallas appeared to have secured control of the contest after taking a 31-10 lead in the third quarter. The Cowboys continued to hold the advantage late in the fourth, leading 38-36 with less than a minute remaining. However, head coach Brian Schottenheimer’s decision on fourth-and-1 created an opportunity for Philadelphia to take control. Rather than attempting to punt or protect the lead through another approach, Dallas kept its offense on the field with 55 seconds remaining. Quarterback Dak Prescott was subsequently sacked for a nine-yard loss, giving the Eagles possession in favorable field position. Philadelphia capitalized on the opportunity, with kicker Jake Elliott converting a 59-yard field goal with two seconds left. WNBA Star Caitlin Clark Reacts to Dallas Cowboys’ Loss to Philadelphia Eagles Indiana Fever guard Caitlin Clark (22) arrives Tuesday, Sept. 16, 2025, before Game 2 of a WNBA playoff matchup between the Indiana Fever and the Atlanta Dream at Gainbridge Fieldhouse in Indianapolis. Clark shared her thoughts about Dallas’ loss to the Eagles on Thanksgiving. This can be seen in a post she shared on X. “What exactly were the cowboys doing there,” Clark wrote. Clark posted a brief question about the Cowboys’ decision , reflecting the confusion shared by many viewers following the sequence. Although she did not identify a particular player or coach in her message, the timing suggested her reaction was connected to Dallas’ costly fourth-down attempt. The defeat was particularly damaging because the Cowboys had controlled much of the matchup before allowing Philadelphia to rally. Clark’s reaction added another prominent name to the growing discussion surrounding Dallas’ Thanksgiving collapse, which left the franchise searching for answers after a painful divisional loss. item.title: Central Bucks West shuts out Spring-Ford, wins district championship
item.description: DOYLESTOWN — Central Bucks West played for its sixth PIAA District One football championship on Friday night. The Bucks won District One onfield titles under Mike Pettine in 1993 and 1997-99, as well as Mike Carey in 2000. Spring-Ford, like CB West, went into the game at War Memorial Field with identical 12-1 records. The Bucks finished the job, downing the Rams 34-0 behind a dominant rushing attack and suffocating defense. Senior Lou Cipollo ran for a pair of touchdowns while seniors Nick Miletto and Braylen Cope both scored a rushing touchdown. CB West will face the St. Joseph Prep/Nazareth winner in next weekend’s Class 6A semifinals. Prep led Nazareth 49-20 at the start of the fourth quarter. West had reached the district title game in 2022, when it lost at Garnet Valley, while Spring-Ford fell to Coatesville for the 2012 district championship. This is the Bucks' first district title in 26 seasons. Rob Rowan’s CB West squad defeated Perkiomen Valley 56-42, Central Bucks East 44-21 and Council Rock South 30-13 to reach the final, while Spring-Ford topped Quakertown 42-28, Plymouth Whitemarsh 28-21 and top-seeded Downingtown East 17-14 at districts. *Check back later tonight for much more on the game. What’s next for Spring-Ford Football? The season ended for the Rams. What’s next for Central Bucks West Football? The Bucks will face St. Joseph Prep or Nazareth in the state semifinals next weekend. Tom Moore: tmoore@couriertimes.com ; @TomMoorePhilly is a sports columnist for PhillyBurbs.com . Support our journalism with a subscription . This article originally appeared on Bucks County Courier Times: Central Bucks West shuts out Spring-Ford, wins district championship

item.title: 2027 Presidential poll: What will influence our votes — Nigerians
item.description: *Torn between Tinubu’s reforms, Obi’s change message, Atiku’s comeback *Say, Tinubu has capacity to take bold decisions, Obi possesses good credentials, Atiku may reduce petrol price By Dayo Johnson, Regional Editor, South West The 2027 general election is barely two months away. Some of the political parties that will be on the ballot have already hit the streets campaigning. Many of the candidates are seeking to renew the mandate that was given to them in 2023. Others who didn’t make it in the last election are back again hoping to succeed this time around. The candidates are making fresh promises. The electorate, on their part, have been speaking on what will inform their choice of who to vote for during the elections and their responses reveal an electorate pulled in sharply different directions. We did not embark on data collation but randomly spoke with some Nigerians in the southwest, southeast, south south and the northern region of the country. Backers of President Bola Tinubu defend him on his capacity to push restructuring and take bold decisions, arguing that but for him the economy would have collapsed completely, even as some concede that his reforms have yet to ease hardship. But they have hope and argue that Nigeria would be better under Tinubu in the years to come. A few voices break from the Obi-Tinubu argument entirely, backing Atiku, the ADC, or local candidates on performance. In markets, campuses and government offices, a strong current of support for Peter Obi runs through everyday voters- market women, traders, students and civil servants, who point to the rising cost of living, government borrowing and hunger for change. Another powerful theme in their responses is the widespread distrust of the electoral system itself. Many voters express lack of faith in the process and expect politicians to rig and litigate rather than accept the people’s verdict, even as the spate of ongoing violence is already scaring them. Professionals frame their choices more cautiously arguing that they will be guided by candidates’ positions on sustainable development, Niger Delta equity and resource justice rather than ethnicity or party. From conviction to civic duty to indecision, the message from the streets is clear: a wary electorate is watching, and waiting to decide amidst fears of violence. Speaking, Amaebi Clarkson, a lawyer in Lagos said: The Campaigns have been intense, with grandiose promises But beyond the rhetoric, Peter Obi obviously has good credentials, with proven track records to make a good pl president. I think he has good intentions for Nigeria and is better poised to positively drive the country. However, I prefer Tinubu to be the president at this crucial time, not because he will bring any tangible development or perform any miracle. item.title: Mangiapane Scores Twice, Blackhawks Beat Rangers For Fourth Straight Win
item.description: The Chicago Blackhawks (10-14-2) tied a franchise record for the fewest shots recorded in a regular-season game with 10, but it was enough to defeat the New York Rangers (13-11-1) 2-1 at the United Center on Friday. Andrew Mangiapane scored both of Chicago’s goals, his first two tallies of the season, Oliver Moore had two assists, and Spencer Knight stopped 30 of 31 shots as the Blackhawks extended their winning streak to four games. The Blackhawks are now 6-1-1 in eight games since an abysmal 0-3 Southeastern road trip earlier this month. Mika Zibanejad scored for the Rangers, while Dylan Garand started in net and allowed two goals on 10 shots faced. Adam Fox extended his point streak to five games with an assist on Zibanejad’s power-play goal. All three goals in Friday’s game were power-play tallies, with the Blackhawks converting on both opportunities and extending their goal streak to eight games. Since opening the season with a 5-for-51 stretch, the power play has now scored on 13 of its last 22 opportunities. Even without Patrick Kane and Tyler Bertuzzi , the man advantage continued its red-hot stretch, and it was the second unit stepping up to score both goals against the Rangers. Entering Friday, New York had the NHL’s top-ranked penalty kill and had allowed a league-low three power-play goals in their first 12 road games. But even without their best offensive players, including captain Connor Bedard and Bowen Byram , the power play impressively still found a way to generate all the offense needed against a stout Rangers’ PK for a fourth straight win. Defensively, Knight was outstanding for the second straight game, as the 25-year-old was credited with 2.03 goals saved above expected against the Rangers. Over his last three outings — all wins — Knight has stopped 92 of 97 shots for a .948 save percentage. While the Rangers outshot and outchanced the Blackhawks by a wide margin, they were credited with only 10 high-danger scoring chances at even strength. Much like Wednesday’s win in Seattle, the Hawks’ defense didn’t allow many threatening looks. The defensemen and forwards also selflessly stepped in the shooting lane, recording 22 blocked shots in Friday’s win. Here are highlights from the Blackhawks 2-1 win over the Rangers, moving their 2026-27 regular-season record to 10-14-2 in 26 games. First Period With Matt Rempe in the penalty box for boarding Kevin Korchinski , the scorching-hot Blackhawks power play hit the ice for the first time and converted. Moore poked a loose puck over to Mangiapane at the right circle, and he fired a one-timer past Garand for his first goal of the season at 4:23. 1-0, Chicago. Oliver Moore➡️Andrew Mangiapane🚨 #Blackhawks extend their power-play streak to 8 games, as Moore gets the puck over to Mangiapane for his 1st goal of the season! 1-0. pic.twitter.com/DhTBlwMrNL — Talkin’ Hawkey (@TalkinHawkey) November 27, 2026 Roughly five minutes later, Dillon Boucher made Rempe answer for his hit on Korchinski. item.title: Jason Kelce Drops Honest Take After Kansas City Chiefs’ Controversial Loss to Buffalo Bills
item.description: Former Philadelphia Eagles center Jason Kelce took a sarcastic shot at the Kansas City Chiefs’ officiating controversy after their narrow Thanksgiving defeat to the Buffalo Bills. Kelce addressed the discussion surrounding a disputed ruling involving Rashee Rice, using the opportunity to revisit complaints about officials allegedly favoring Kansas City. The Chiefs suffered a 13-10 loss at Highmark Stadium after both teams struggled to generate consistent offensive production in difficult conditions. However, one fourth-quarter decision became a major talking point after officials overturned what initially appeared to be a crucial Rice reception. Feb 4, 2024; Orlando, FL, USA; NFC center Jason Kelce (62) of the Philadelphia Eagles before the 2024 Pro Bowl at Camping World Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-USA TODAY Sports Patrick Mahomes connected with Rice on third-and-10 with less than two minutes remaining in regulation. The receiver appeared to secure an 11-yard catch, which would have given Kansas City a first down and an opportunity to continue its potential game-winning possession. Officials initially ruled the play a completion before a review determined that Rice had lost control of the football while going to the ground. The reversal forced the Chiefs into a fourth-and-long situation near their own end zone, eventually leading to a punt. Kansas City head coach Andy Reid questioned the decision afterward, suggesting the available replay evidence did not clearly justify overturning the original ruling. The call became an immediate source of frustration among the franchise’s fans and former NFL players. Jason Kelce Drops Honest Take After Kansas City Chiefs’ Controversial Loss to Buffalo Bills Oct 20, 2025; Detroit, Michigan, USA; ESPN broadcaster Jason Kelce before the game between the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and the Detroit Lions at Ford Field. Mandatory Credit: David Reginek-Imagn Images Kelce shared a blunt take after Kansas City loses to the Bills recently. This can be seen in a post he made on X. “Well, at least we don’t have to hear all of twitter bitch about the refs being homers for the Chiefs tonight,” Kelce wrote. Kelce responded on social media with a sarcastic remark about the recurring accusations that referees favor Kansas City. His message suggested that the controversial decision would make it difficult for critics to continue claiming the Chiefs receive favorable treatment from officials. The former center’s reaction quickly became part of the broader discussion surrounding the game. The Chiefs ultimately failed to overcome the setback, while Buffalo secured the 13-10 victory. Kelce’s comments added another dimension to the officiating debate, which has followed Kansas City through several closely contested games. item.title: 3 Observations from Indiana men’s basketball’s 93-57 win over Bowling Green
item.description: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - NOVEMBER 9: Darian DeVries, head coach of the Indiana Hoosiers coaches during the game against the Syracuse Orange at Gainbridge Fieldhouse on November 9, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Michael Hickey/Getty Images) | Getty Images Indiana men’s basketball dominated Bowling Green tonight, going on a run just over five minutes into the game that effectively put the Falcons to bed. The Hoosiers were shooting well, defending well, and rebounding well in what may have been the most complete performance from this group so far. Though it wasn’t a marquee win like last week’s victories over Arkansas or Kentucky, the margin of victory was one that boosted Indiana’s computer profile. KenPom only favored Indiana by 20 entering the game, so the blowout moved Indiana up five spots in the national ranking. At 8-0, Indiana looks much improved over Darian DeVries’ first season, with KenPom now projecting the Hoosiers to win 23 games and go 12-8 in Big Ten play. Here are 3 Observations from the win: Ball Movement Indiana had a season-high 18 assists tonight against Bowling Green, starting to resemble the fast-paced offense we saw from DeVries’ group last year. While Indiana has more players that are capable of creating unassisted buckets, the ball movement tonight helped the Hoosiers take more quality looks from the perimeter, something that will be important for maintaining a respectable 3-point percentage this season. Bryce Lindsay’s deep shot against Arkansas will go down as a high-point of the season, but over the last couple games Indiana had gotten into the habit of chucking a few too many heat checks from deep or taking transition threes that negate the team’s rebounding advantage. Seeing the way the ball moved tonight was an encouraging step for this group not just cause it made the offense look a little better, but because it reflects well on the team’s chemistry so early in the season. With a team full of transfers, having nine different players record an assist in a game is no small feat. Aiden Sherrell Aiden Sherrell had one of his stronger performances of the season, finishing with 16 points, nine rebounds, two blocks and an assist. He also went 2-6 from 3-point range. Tonight’s performance was a good example of why he’s a potential NBA player. A seven footer who can score from the perimeter, rebound on both ends of the floor, and protect the rim is a valuable piece for any team. After an impressive year last year at Bama, he’s averaging more points and shooting better from deep this year at Indiana. Even though he cooled off by the end of the night, his early threes are exactly what Indiana will need from him going forward. Establishing himself as a threat at the beginning of the game will force defenses to account for him until the final whistle. item.title: Michael Strahan Reacts to Aaron Rodgers’ Controversial Take About Pittsburgh Steelers Coach Mike McCarthy
item.description: Pro Football Hall of Famer Michael Strahan delivered a harsh assessment of Aaron Rodgers following the quarterback’s public criticism of Pittsburgh Steelers coach Mike McCarthy. The former New York Giants defensive end questioned Rodgers’ decision to discuss internal team issues publicly, arguing that his comments ultimately hurt the organization. Strahan addressed the controversy during Fox’s Thanksgiving pregame coverage, joining several former players and analysts who had criticized Rodgers’ appearance on The Pat McAfee Show. The quarterback had discussed his strained relationship with McCarthy after being benched, sharing several complaints about the coach’s preparation and leadership. May 28, 2026; Pittsburgh, PA, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers (8) participates in OTA drills at the UPMC Rooney Sports Complex. Mandatory Credit: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images Rodgers alleged that McCarthy arrived late to meetings and occasionally fell asleep during team sessions. He also questioned aspects of the coach’s playcalling and described frustration with the team’s direction. The interview attracted significant attention because Rodgers had spent years working with McCarthy during their time with the Green Bay Packers before their relationship deteriorated. Strahan acknowledged that McCarthy might not be entirely blameless in the disagreement. However, he argued that Rodgers should have handled the situation privately instead of bringing the conflict into a public setting. The former defensive end emphasized that football remains a team sport and that players should consider how their actions affect teammates and coaches. Michael Strahan Reacts to Aaron Rodgers’ Controversial Take About Pittsburgh Steelers Coach Mike McCarthy May 25, 2025; Indianapolis, Indiana, USA; Michael Strahan in attendance during the 109th Running of the Indianapolis 500 at Indianapolis Motor Speedway. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Strahan shared his thoughts about Rodgers amid Pittsbugh’s decision to release him. This can be seen in a video shared by Fox Sports: NFL on X. Michael Strahan provides his reaction to Aaron Rodgers’ comments before being released by Pittsburgh @michaelstrahan https://t.co/BafFkaIruo — FOX Sports: NFL (@NFLonFOX) November 26, 2026 The criticism became particularly personal when Strahan addressed Rodgers’ explanation that his career earnings allowed him to speak freely. The former Giants star took issue with the quarterback using his financial success to justify publicly discussing the disagreement. He argued that Rodgers’ approach reflected poorly on his attitude as a teammate, regardless of whether some of his complaints about McCarthy were justified. Pittsburgh subsequently released Rodgers following the interview, ending his time with the organization after the benching controversy. item.title: Rutgers Women’s Basketball Suffers First Loss of Season, 84-68 to South Dakota State
item.description: Mia Pauldo of the Rutgers Scarlet Knights possesses the ball during an NCAA women's basketball game at Jersey Mike's Arena in Piscataway, United States, on November 16, 2026. (Photo by Dan Squicciarini/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images After starting the season 8-0 and defeating cross-state rival Princeton, Rutgers women’s basketball suffered its first loss of the season, 84-68 to South Dakota State in game one of the Daytona Beach Classic. The Scarlet Knights got off to an ugly start in this game, where they could not dig themselves out of a steep first-quarter hole that saw them down 21 points after just 10 minutes of play. After the game was tied at 5 with just over 8 minutes to play in the first quarter, South Dakota State would go on a 12-0 run to go up 17-5 before the Knights scored again around the four-minute mark in the first quarter. Rutgers would string together four points before the Jackrabbits went on a 13-0 run to close out the quarter up 30-9. The Knights would start to get off the mat over the next two quarters, preventing South Dakota from going on unanswered runs as they did in the first quarter, and eventually closing the gap to single digits as they headed into the fourth quarter down 63-54. However, for every shot the Knights made in the fourth quarter, the Jackrabbits had an answer. A quick three-pointer by South Dakota State’s Hadley Thul at the start of the fourth would put Rutgers in another double-digit hole, one they could not recover from, as the Jackrabbits held on to secure the win. This game highlights some early-season concerns for the Knights, who allowed the Jackrabbits to hit 49.2 percent of their total shots and 52 percent of their shots from three. On top of that, the Jackrabbits forced six more turnovers. recorded 14 more rebounds, had six more points in the paint, and had 15 more assists in their winning effort. Brooklyn Meyer led the Jackrabbits with 20 points, with Katie Vasecka right behind her at 19. Meyer recorded a double-double on the day by scooping up 10 rebounds as well. Emilee Fox and Mali Abdouch recorded double-digit points for South Dakota State as well. Mia Pauldo was once again the star of the show for Rutgers, recording 37 points and hitting half of her shots. In addition to their poor defensive performance, the Knights, outside of Pauldo, failed to drum up any offensive consistency. Outside of Pauldo’s 14 of 28 on all her shots, the rest of the Knights hit just nine of their 38 total shots. While Pauldo is a very effective offensive weapon, scoring has to come from other areas to supplement her efforts. The good news is that the Knights still have time to remedy these issues before Big Ten play starts in full force. The next four games against Georgetown, St. Peter’s, No.19 Ohio State and Seton Hall will provide a glimpse into what the Knights will look like for the rest of the season. Rutgers will play Georgetown tomorrow in game two of the Daytona Beach Classic. Tip-

item.title: UNC loses ugly, sloppy game to West Virginia
item.description: Nov 27, 2026; Charlotte, North Carolina, USA; North Carolina Tar Heels head coach Michael Malone pleads his case with the official during the first half against the West Virginia Mountaineers at the Dick Vitale Invitational at Spectrum Center. Mandatory Credit: Jim Dedmon-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Carolina played the part of a turkey hangover on Friday in an ugly 72-59 loss to West Virginia in the Dick Vitale Invitational. The Tar Heels never led, and even when they tried to mount a comeback in the second half, the Mountaineers promptly stepped on their throats and ended the threat. The tale of the tape really starts and ends with turnovers. Carolina turned the ball over 20 times, directly leading to 28 West Virginia points. Terrence Brown committed eight of those turnovers in a brutal game for a guy the Tar Heels have come to rely on for points. He managed just six on 3-7 shooting. UNC and WVU shot exactly the same percentage from the field at 45%, and Carolina actually made a couple more (11 vs 9) three-pointers. West Virginia had 18 free throw attempts to UNC’s three. The Mountaineers had 14 steals and 11 second chance points. Maximo Adams led the Heels in points 16 points ahead of Jaydon Young with 13 points. Matt Able was scoreless in the first half before hitting a string of three-pointers late to give him 12 points for the game. The highlight of the game for the Tar Heels came when they went on a 12-0 run to cut the deficit to seven points in the second half. West Virginia responded right away with a big run of their own to promptly end any hope that Carolina might steal one they probably had no business stealing. They trailed by as many as 19 halfway through the second half. It has been clear that rebounding is a real issue for this team, and that was on display again tonight. Even though they finished the game only -1 on the boards, there were so many opportunities to keep WVU from getting multiple cracks at a shot or hands that seemed allergic to holding onto a ball. It wasn’t the primary issue in this one (see: turnovers) but it continues to be a real issue. The lack of a real point guard also felt especially prevalent in this mess of a game. Carolina finds itself at the beginning of a considerable stretch of games against Power 4 competition. So far, we’ve seen the games against Georgia and West Virginia end poorly. They’ll face Arkansas in their next game as part of the ACC/SEC challenge. The Razorbacks are coming off a three-point loss to #11 Michigan State.

item.title: Broncos’ Nik Bonitto gets 100% real on getting ‘whooped’ by Steelers
item.description: Barry Reeger-Imagn Images Broncos’ Nik Bonitto gets 100% real on getting ‘whooped’ by Steelers appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . As the Denver Broncos delivered a disappointing 27-5 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers on Friday, there’s no denying that the team got humbled after winning the last six games. With the Broncos’ loss led by a down outing from quarterback Bo Nix , linebacker Nik Bonitto would speak candidly about Denver’s performance as a whole. Speaking after the defeat in his post-game press conference in the locker room, Bonitto kept it real about how Pittsburgh beat the Broncos on Friday. “They just came out and whooped us,” Bonitto said, according to Zac Stevens. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Nik Bonitto: “They just came out and whooped us” pic.twitter.com/rYoUtpFOpH — Zac Stevens (@ZacStevens) November 27, 2026 There’s no doubt that all eyes will be on Denver’s offense, as they only scored three points the entire game, with the other two coming on a safety in the second quarter. Looking at Nix, he threw for 169 yards and two interceptions, but head coach Sean Payton would take full accountability for the loss. “Well, obviously, disappointing loss…it starts with me,” Payton said, via Stevens. “You know, I felt like our prep coming into this week, relative to the schedule, was good. You know, we knew it was going to be a tough challenge coming in here; they played well at home, and I think early on, we gave them opportunities of momentum, and that falls on me.” Sean Payton following the Broncos 27-5 loss. “Disappointing loss… it starts with me” pic.twitter.com/w2j08pe7K4 — Zac Stevens (@ZacStevens) November 27, 2026 The Broncos struggled in all areas, with Nix giving the Steelers many opportunities to flourish, such as a fumble that led to a touchdown for T.J. Watt and a pick-six by Jalen Ramsey towards the end of the first half. At any rate, Denver looks to improve with Dec. 6’s matchup against the Miami Dolphins. item.title: Bills Take Down Chiefs Despite Allen’s Struggles on Thanksgiving Day
item.description: The Buffalo Bills are always going to go as far as superstar quarterback Josh Allen takes them, but that doesn’t mean they can’t win big games without a huge performance from him . On Thursday , Buffalo proved that again, defeating Patrick Mahomes and the visiting Kansas City Chiefs to the tune of a 13-10 score at Highmark Stadium in Orchard Park. Allen was thankful that his teammates still made things happen that allowed Buffalo to overcome his subpar showing. “I have to better. I need to be better. I will be better,” the former NFL Most Valuable Player Allen said after the game, via John Wawrow of the Associated Press . “Thankful for my team. Thankful for my defense. Thankful for my kicker. Thankful for James Cook and our O-linemen. This took a lot of people,” he added. “I made it a little harder on ourselves. But we found a way to get (win No.) 10.” Bills Take Down Chiefs Despite Allen’s Struggles on Thanksgiving Day Nov 26, 2026; Orchard Park, New York, USA; Allen (17) scrambles with the ball against the Chiefs during the third quarter at New Highmark Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark Konezny-Imagn Images Allen only passed for 81 yards with zero touchdowns, while getting picked twice on 10/21 pass completions. But Buffalo’s offense got 117 rushing yards and a touchdown from James Cook III on 32 carries, while the defense held Mahomes to just 174 passing yards on 16/29 completions with zero scores. Allen isn’t always going to be at the top of his game, so it was great for Buffalo to see the other units and players stepping up and delivering the goods when the team’s most important player is struggling. Hopefully for Allen and the Bills, he’ll recover his form in Week 13 against the New England Patriots on the road. item.title: Blue Jackets shut out by Red Wings, booed: 'You've got to push back'
item.description: The booing began with just under three minutes left Nov. 27 at Nationwide Arena. It emanated from the upper reaches of the building and cascaded to the ice during the Blue Jackets' 2-0 loss to the Detroit Red Wings . More: Devils drop Blue Jackets in shootout: Where's the fight? Down two goals, the Blue Jackets had just sent goalie Jet Greaves to the bench for a last gasp 6-on-5 advantage that fans quickly realized was an exercise in futility, much like the home team's play throughout its Black Friday matinee. Things went as expected from there, ending with the Red Wings finally putting an end to a torturous afternoon. Neither team was good, but the Blue Jackets (9-14-1) were, by far, worse. It was their third straight loss, fifth straight loss at home and they're 10 points out of a playoff spot on Thanksgiving weekend, which has become a benchmark for most the NHL's eventual playoff field. Saying the collective mood of the Blue Jackets right now is grim is putting it kindly. There are 60 games remaining and Columbus is lacking two things that typically go arm-in-arm: a pulse and goals. Remarkably, this was the first time they Jackets have been shut out this season despite ranking last in the NHL while scoring 2.33 goals per game. "It's impossible not to think about it," center Adam Fantilli said. "Like, we can hear our fans booing. It's not like we're deaf. Like, we understand the situation. We understand how frustrating it is for them. We're just as frustrated. We're trying to figure it out. We're trying to do everything we can, and it's not going for us." The problem, as seen from the seats, press box and television broadcast, is that it often doesn't look like the Blue Jackets are doing everything they can. Too many times, they look like a team playing out the string, and their level of pushback looks empty. An opposing player lights up a teammate with a cheap shot and the ice doesn't become a yard sale of discarded gloves and sticks. An opposing team sets out to keep the Blue Jackets out of the most dangerous scoring areas and finds it all too easy to accomplish. That's without mentioning the litany of fumbled passes, pucks hopping over sticks, passes sent into a teammate's skates, passes sent to nobody in particular and shots that accomplish nothing but dusting snow off the puck. All of these afflictions were on full display against the Red Wings, who used their impressive size on the back end to clog up the middle of their defensive zone and push the Blue Jackets to the perimeter most of the game. The result was a glaring statistical anomaly on the scoresheet, which showed the Red Wings with a 21-18 edge in shots and the Jackets with a 62-42 edge in attempts. How does that even happen? "I think part of it's a credit to them," Blue Jackets defenseman Zach Werenski said. "They did a good job of standing in our [shooting] lanes, but we've got to find a way to get pucks to the net, get second and third chances, and find a way to score. We had

item.title: Metcalf Makes Wholesome Gesture in Show of Support For Former Steelers Star QB Rodgers
item.description: Aaron Rodgers is no longer with the Pittsburgh Steelers , but it appears that he is very much in the heart of wide receiver DK Metcalf. The hulking Pittsburgh wideout made his presence felt late in the first quarter of Friday’s game against the visiting Denver Broncos at Acrisure Stadium in Pittsburgh when he scored a 22-yard touchdown off a pass from Rodgers’ replacement under center, Mason Rudolph. The touchdown extended Pittsburgh’s lead to 14-0 following a made extra-point kick from kicker Chris Boswell. But Metcalf turned even more heads when he seemingly showed some love to Rodgers with a series of hand gestures that translate to “Stand on business, eight,” as interpreted by American Sign Language. Here is a video of that moment in the end zone: With the help of @hawkmania4 , it looks like, after his TD, DK Metcalf signed: “Stand on business, 8.” https://t.co/5keziYBDJU pic.twitter.com/rokjOpssrU — Arye Pulli (@AryePulliNFL) November 27, 2026 Metcalf Makes Wholesome Gesture in Show of Support For Former Steelers Star QB Rodgers Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers (8) throws a pass during an NFL football game against the Cleveland Browns at Acrisure Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Barry Reeger-Imagn Images That was quite a statement from Metcalf amid the fallout from the bitter breakup between Pittsburgh and the four-time NFL Most Valuable Player Rodgers, who might already played his last game in the league. Many didn’t feel right with the way Rodgers handled himself on the way out of Pittsburgh, but Metcalf at least appears to be in support of his now-former QB. That doesn’t mean Metcalf’s loyalty isn’t on the Steelers. He doesn’t have to pick sides, and his gesture could simply be a way of showing Rodgers that he holds no grudges against him. Now in his second season with Pittsburgh, Metcalf entered Week 12 with 434 receiving yards and two touchdowns on 36 receptions and 74 targets. item.title: St. John’s men’s basketball gets gritty win over Iowa State in their Players Era Festival finale
item.description: Nov 27, 2026; Las Vegas, NV, USA; St. John's Red Storm guard Tounde Yessoufou (24) steals the ball during a third place game of the Players Era Sixteen tournament at Michelob Ultra Arena. Mandatory Credit: Candice Ward-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Just a dozen hours after battling back from a 24-point deficit only to fall heartbreakingly at the buzzer against Louisville, the Red Storm showed their resilience against Iowa State and added a fantastic early-season win to their résumé. St. John’s overcame a nine-point first-half deficit and gutted out an 80-75 win over Iowa State, ending their Players Era trip on a high note with a 2-1 record. Both teams struggled to find a rhythm in a game that tipped off at 10 a.m. local time, combining for 44 turnovers, with the Red Storm accounting for 21 of those giveaways. Ian Jackson carried the St. John’s offense by scoring 11 of their first 18 points, but Iowa State mounted a 12-0 run to take a 27-18 lead. Despite shooting 15-of-28 from the field and doubling Iowa State on rebounds, the Cyclones rode into the break with a 40-38 lead. T.J. Otzelberger’s team capitalized on a dozen Red Storm turnovers and porous rim protection from Reed Bailey, who replaced Ruben Prey after the Johnnies’ starting center committed two quick fouls to open the game. Iowa State big man Dominyka Pleta led the way with 12 points on a perfect 5-of-5 shooting heading into the locker room. Unlike last night’s game against Louisville, the Red Storm responded quickly after the second half began. Following a pair of Tre Singleton baskets, the Red Storm went on a 13-0 run to capture a 52-44 lead and didn’t relinquish it. Ruben Prey stayed out of foul trouble and provided enough interior resistance to keep Iowa State from another big run. 11-0 run for the Johnnies‼️ pic.twitter.com/xN9vNqHIIA — St. John's Men’s Basketball (@StJohnsBBall) November 27, 2026 Tounde Yessoufou exemplified St. John’s’ dogged effort, battling through an illness and scoring 18 of his team-high 23 points after the 10:17 mark in the second half, including the final seven points of the game for the Red Storm. The future NBA draft pick did everything he could to ensure St. John’s left Las Vegas with a second win, recording a team-high eight rebounds, six steals, four assists, and three blocks. According to CBS Sports Research, Yessoufou became the second player in the last 30 years to put up that stat line against a high-major opponent. Tounde triple 🔥 pic.twitter.com/RlFKJo2zPv — St. John's Men’s Basketball (@StJohnsBBall) November 27, 2026 Friday’s win over Iowa State was the Red Storm’s highest-ranked KenPom non-conference victory since dispatching Arizona on December 21, 2019, when Arizona was ranked 14th. The Cyclones entered as the 18th-ranked team in the country by KenPom. On Friday, November 27, WWE announced to the professional wrestling world that Jermaine Haley, better known to fans as Bronson Reed , had passed away at just 38 years old. Sharing the news on social media before it broke anywhere else, WWE revealed that Reed had passed away due to medical complications and sent their condolences to his young family and wife Paige, who is currently pregnant. “WWE is devastated to announce that Jermaine Haley, also known as Bronson Reed , passed away earlier today at the age of 38 due to medical complications,” WWE wrote. “Jermaine was a larger-than-life figure in WWE, but more importantly, he was a phenomenal person, a devoted family man, and a beloved colleague. Our thoughts and deepest condolences are with Jermaine’s entire family, including his pregnant wife, Paige, their daughter, as well as his friends, co-workers, and fans.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) WWE is devastated to announce that Jermaine Haley, known to WWE fans as Bronson Reed, passed away earlier today. Our thoughts and deepest condolences are with Jermaine’s family, friends and fans. pic.twitter.com/5ttxdSi3kb — WWE (@WWE) November 28, 2026 One of the landmark wrestlers from Australia who helped to open the door for younger stars like Grayson Waller, Kyler Fletcher, and Rhea Ripley, Bronson was in the middle of his second tenure in WWE, with stops in TNA, Pro Wrestling Noah, PWG, and New Japan Pro Wrestling, where he briefly led the TMDK stable as Jonah Rock, along his storied career. After being written off WWE television at Crown Jewel, where he was injured when Oba Femi threw him off the stage onto a table , Reed was honored by the promotion with two 10-bell salutes at the promotion’s two Friday night house shows, in addition to a graphic displayed on SmackDown along with WWE’s condolences. item.title: Jazz Chisholm Jr. Signs One-Year Deal With Blue Jays
item.description: Jonathan Dyer-Imagn Images Jazz Chisholm Jr. has left the New York Yankees to join their AL East rival, the Toronto Blue Jays. ESPN reported on Friday afternoon that the two-time All-Star signed a one-year contract worth $20 million. A $16 million player option for the 2028 season and a $6 million signing bonus are part of the deal. This move keeps Chisholm in the division while shifting him to a team that finished last in the East last year. The contract structure offers a unique twist for the 28-year-old infielder. Should Chisholm decline his $16 million player option next year, Toronto’s deal becomes a $40 million team option. This clause gives the player leverage while providing the Blue Jays with a safety net if they wish to retain him long-term. The signing comes as the Yankees face uncertainty in their own lineup construction for the upcoming season. Chisholm’s Recent Performance and Value Chisholm brings a mix of power and speed to Toronto , though his 2026 numbers were modest. He hit 19 home runs and drove in 55 runs while stealing 41 bases for the Yankees last season. His batting line ended at .231/.312/.399, which resulted in 1.7 wins above replacement. These figures show a player who still generates runs but struggled to find consistent contact in the previous year. The year before, in 2025, Chisholm posted much stronger results, earning him a Silver Slugger Award. He recorded 31 home runs, 80 RBIs, and 31 stolen bases with a .481 slugging percentage. That performance proved he could be a top-tier contributor when healthy and in rhythm. The Blue Jays hope he can return to that form after moving to a new ballpark and lineup. Chisholm has played multiple positions throughout his career, adding flexibility to his contract value. He started with the Miami Marlins as a shortstop and center fielder before the trade to New York. During his time in the Bronx, he played third base and second base. This versatility allows Toronto to plug him into various spots in their infield mix alongside Ernie Clement and Andrés Giménez. The Yankees’ Reaction to the Loss The departure of a key infielder leaves a gap for the Yankees to fill before spring training. General Manager Brian Cashman has been open about the lack of guarantees for the upcoming roster. In mid-November at Yankee Stadium, Cashman stood on the field and acknowledged that “it makes no sense to guarantee anybody anything right now.” This statement reflects the team’s cautious approach after 17 years without a championship. Cashman also addressed the possibility of using younger players to fill the void left by Chisholm. He was asked specifically about Spencer Jones and whether the team felt ready to put him in center field next season. Cashman responded by saying, “I think he best profiles in the corner, but am I comfortable enough if things were as they are currently that he would be in center? I would be comfortable with that,” Cashman said last week. This comment suggests the team is wi

item.title: Recap: Boston College falls to Cincinnati, 70-59
item.description: BOSTON, MASSACHUSETTS - NOVEMBER 06: Brandon Benjamin #20 of the Boston College Eagles high-fives his teammates after being taken out of a game against the Massachusetts Minutemen during the second half at the TD Garden on November 06, 2026 in Boston, Massachusetts. (Photo by Brian Fluharty/Getty Images) | Getty Images On Friday afternoon, the Boston College men’s basketball team faced Cincinnati in its second and final game of the ESPN Events Invitational at State Farm Field House in Kissimmee, FL. BC came in 7-0, a day removed from a last-second win over UCF, and as a 9.5-point underdog. The Bearcats handed BC its first loss of the season, 70-59, pulling away in the second half. The start was promising. Tyler Tejada hit two early threes to put Cincinnati up 6-1, but BC turned five Bearcat turnovers into a 13-0 run and led 14-6 after a Money Williams layup at the 12:14 mark. Williams scored 10 points during that stretch. Then the offense dried up. Former BC forward Jayden Hastings started a Cincinnati run with two free throws, and the Bearcats took a 20-19 lead on an Elijah Perryman layup with just over five minutes left in the half. The teams traded baskets until two Armoni Zeigler free throws gave BC a 28-27 halftime lead. Cincinnati committed 10 turnovers in the first half, and BC held an 11-3 edge in points off turnovers at the break. That’s the primary reason BC was ahead. Cincinnati cleaned that up after halftime. A Colby Duggan three put BC up 31-29, but the Bearcats scored the next six to lead 35-31. Williams tied it at 36 with a second-chance three at 15:18. Cincinnati then went on a 12-2 run, capped by a Tylen Riley steal and breakaway dunk, to lead 48-38 with 10:54 left. BC never got even again. To BC’s credit, it didn’t go away. Down 52-42 with 9:02 left, BC scored five straight through Williams while Cincinnati went 3:37 without a point. Duggan’s corner three later cut it to 60-57 with 3:06 left, and BC had a real chance. Tejada ended it. He answered with a three from the right wing to make it 63-57, then hit another from the top of the key to make it 66-59 with 1:34 left. After Williams missed a three, Tejada grabbed the rebound and made both free throws to push the lead to nine. Cincinnati closed on a 10-2 spurt. Tejada finished with a game-high 24 points, 18 of them in the second half, on 7/11 shooting, 4/5 from three and 6/6 at the line. The shooting numbers tell most of the story. BC shot 17/57 from the field, while Cincinnati shot 23/45. The Bearcats won the paint 28-12 and the bench 24-6. Cincinnati shot 56.5% after halftime, which is not something BC’s defense had allowed much of through seven games. BC grabbed 17 offensive rebounds and got 14 second-chance points out of them, which kept the game close longer than it probably should have been. Hastings, who played 62 games over two seasons at BC, had a quiet but useful game against his old team, with 7 points, 5 rebounds and 3 blocks off the bench. Perryman added 6 points, 5

item.title: Matt Rempe Fights After Boarding in Rangers vs Blackhawks
item.description: Matt Rempe Fights After Brutal Hit in Rangers vs Blackhawks Getty SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - NOVEMBER 07: Jaroslav Chmelar #49 of the New York Rangers celebrates with Marcus Pettersson #26 of the New York Rangers and Matt Rempe #73 of the New York Rangers after scoring against the Seattle Kraken during the first period at Climate Pledge Arena on November 07, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Olivia Vanni/Getty Images) Getty The New York Rangers are trying to keep the good times rolling against the Chicago Blackhawks. Matt Rempe is also doing his best to stay in the lineup. Tonight, he laid a big hit on Kevin Korchinski and then answered the bell with a fight. “ WE’VE GOT A FRIDAY EVENING TILT ON THE MENU,” Sportsnet shared on social media. WE'VE GOT A FRIDAY EVENING TILT ON THE MENU 🥊 pic.twitter.com/8fyK32tAbu — Sportsnet (@Sportsnet) November 27, 2026 Looking at Matt Rempe’s Impact On The New York Rangers Getty SEATTLE, WASHINGTON – NOVEMBER 07: Jaroslav Chmelar #49 of the New York Rangers celebrates with Marcus Pettersson #26 of the New York Rangers and Matt Rempe #73 of the New York Rangers after scoring against the Seattle Kraken during the first period at Climate Pledge Arena on November 07, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Olivia Vanni/Getty Images) Standing 6-foot-9, the Rangers forward brings a level of size and toughness that few players around the NHL can match. Whether he’s dropping the gloves, delivering big hits or getting involved in scrums, Rempe has made his presence felt whenever he’s on the ice. One of the biggest parts of Rempe’s game has been his willingness to fight. Since making his NHL debut in February 2024, he has become known for taking on some of the league’s toughest players. His fights have helped energize the Madison Square Garden crowd while giving the Rangers a player willing to stand up for his teammates. Rempe’s physical play also extends beyond fighting. He uses his size to finish checks, create space along the boards and make life difficult for opposing defensemen. While his offensive production remains a work in progress, Rempe provides something different to the Rangers lineup. His combination of size, toughness and willingness to play a physical game gives New York an added element that opponents have to account for every night. item.title: Important warning emerges for all teams pursuing Simon Edvinsson
item.description: Important warning emerges for all teams pursuing Simon Edvinsson The trade speculation surrounding Simon Edvinsson continues to heat up, but a new report suggests that landing the Detroit Red Wings defenseman may be considerably more complicated than interested teams initially anticipated. With the Dec. 1 deadline approaching, several NHL clubs have reportedly been monitoring Edvinsson's situation. The Edmonton Oilers have emerged as a particularly intriguing potential destination, while the Boston Bruins have also been mentioned as a team to watch. However, according to a recent report, there is one major obstacle standing in the way of a potential blockbuster deal: Edvinsson's next contract. Speaking about the situation, Elliotte Friedman explained that he isn't convinced the defenseman would necessarily agree to sign with every team that has been connected to him. More importantly, several interested clubs reportedly want assurances that they can secure Edvinsson on a long-term contract before giving up significant assets to acquire him. "There are a couple of places they've talked more about a bridge than a long-term deal," the insider explained, adding that teams aren't willing to surrender valuable players without a longer commitment from the Swedish defenseman. https://x.com/RinkyReport/status/2125651414193983837 That creates a difficult situation for Detroit. The Red Wings may be able to find interested trade partners, but those clubs could be reluctant to meet the asking price without knowing exactly what they're getting in return. Edvinsson has established himself as an important part of Detroit's blue line, making him a valuable trade target. However, his contract situation makes any potential deal considerably riskier. For Edmonton and the other teams reportedly keeping tabs on the situation, the question is no longer simply whether they can acquire Edvinsson. It's whether they can convince him to stay for the long haul. With the deadline approaching, that uncertainty could become the biggest obstacle in what has quickly turned into one of the NHL's most intriguing trade stories.

item.title: Ducks lose momentum of early Solberg strikes, can't find push against Kings
item.description: Stian Solberg #50 of the Anaheim Ducks throws his hands up after a call during an NHL regular season game against the Los Angeles Kings on November 27, 2026 at Honda Center in Anaheim, California. ANAHEIM, Calif. – In a game that turned all hockey-watching eyes of Norway toward Honda Center, the Anaheim Ducks squandered a strong start against their rivals and could not make a late push. Stian Solberg scored his first two NHL goals in the first period, but countryman Mats Zuccarello matched with two sharp-angle goals in the second period. The Los Angeles Kings grabbed the lead on an early third-period deflection and held off the Ducks, 5-3, on Friday at Honda Center. Anaheim (12-13-1, 25 points) has lost seven of its last nine following a five-game winning streak. This was just the Ducks’ fourth total loss when scoring three or more goals (12-3-1), and they are winless when scoring two or fewer (0-11-0). “We got ourselves on our heels there early in the second,” Joel Quenneville said. “They scored two goals, funny goals, and they slowed down the pace. We were skating well in the first period, and I think we got standing around there a bit.” Anaheim, kings of the late-game comeback last season, are just 3-3-0 when tied after two periods and 1-10-0 when trailing after 40 minutes. The Ducks–who thought they had scored with the goalie pulled, but the referees blew the play dead and upheld that call on review–are second in the NHL in extra-attacker goals with five, but each has come in a regulation loss. “We haven’t been able to do that lately,” Mikael Granlund said. “We’ve got to find another gear when it comes time. Something we gotta do better.” “I don’t think that’s the recipe for being successful,” Quenneville said, “coming back late in games thinking that’s going to work. Eventually it can catch up to you. Certainly, we were charmed in some of those games last year.” After a traditionally sleepy start to this traditional Black Friday matinee, Stian Solberg woke up Honda Center with his first two deposits on his NHL ledger. Mikael Granlund sliced the defensive zone with a diagonal pass to Solberg at the right point, where the Norwegian faked out countryman Mats Zuccarello and ripped a shot far side around the kneeling King for the lead, 1-0. “That was a special moment for me,” Solberg said, “and a lot of fun to put that in the back of the net. That’s probably something I’m going to remember for a long time… It was kind of funny it was him. I’m probably going to shoot (Zuccarello) a text.” Solberg’s first career NHL goal put him as the third Norwegian defenseman to score an NHL goal, joining Emil Lilleberg and Ole-Kristian Tollefsen. Lilleberg, currently on the Tampa Bay blue line, has scored five in his NHL career, and Tollefsen netted four for the Columbus Blue Jackets. item.title: Bills Clock Operator Under Fire After Video of Controversial Chiefs Ending Surfaces
item.description: Some are questioning the ending of Thursday's Thanksgiving game between the Buffalo Bills and Kansas City Chiefs Getty The Bills celebrate Tyler Bass' game-winning field goal against the Chiefs Getty Kansas City Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes Getty Josh Allen throws a pass against the Kansas City Chiefs on Thanksgiving. The Buffalo Bills have been on the wrong end of a few seconds against the Kansas City Chiefs before. This time, the clock might have worked in their favor. First-year head coach Joe Brady and the Bills improved to 10-1 with a 13-10 win over the Chiefs on Thanksgiving night, when kicker Tyler Bass hit a 57-yard field goal as time expired. A day later, the talk has moved from Bass’ leg to the Highmark Stadium game clock. Several analysts believe Buffalo’s clock operator gave the Bills extra time on Kansas City’s final drive. There’s also video that appears to back them up. Bills’ Clock Operator Accused of Adding Time Getty The Bills celebrate Tyler Bass’ game-winning field goal against the Chiefs The Chiefs took over at their own 11-yard line with 26 seconds left in a tie game, and the Bills still had all three timeouts. On first down, quarterback Patrick Mahomes dropped the shotgun snap and fell on it, and Buffalo called timeout. When play resumed, the clock read 25 seconds. Sharp Football Analysis founder Warren Sharp wasn’t buying it, offering video proof that something fishy happened. “We need to talk about the clock in the final 26 seconds of the Bills-Chiefs game,” Sharp posted on X. “It was reset after MULTIPLE plays to add time and NEVER was discussed. How much time? A total of 7 seconds. Just enough time after the punt to put 4 seconds on the clock & allow a game-winning Bills FG.” VIDEO PROOF of a massive blunder last night we need to talk about the clock in the final 26 seconds of the Bills-Chiefs game it was reset after MULTIPLE plays to add time and NEVER was discussed how much time? a total of 7 seconds just enough time after the punt to put 4… pic.twitter.com/u7QC2OITKu — Warren Sharp (@SharpFootball) November 27, 2026 Sharp pointed to NBC’s Mike Tirico, who told viewers that Brady was “running down to take a timeout and they get it with 19 seconds left.” He said the clock got bumped up again, from 19 to 20, after running back Emmett Johnson’s 5-yard run on second down. Bills’ FG Made Possible Because of Extra Time Added? Getty Kansas City Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes Pro Football Talk’s Mike Florio counted four extra seconds . He said the clock showed 15 seconds after a third-down incompletion when it should have shown 11. That matters. Linebacker Joe Andreessen tipped the ensuing punt. Greg Dortch returned it to the Kansas City 39-yard line with four seconds left. That was just enough for Bass to win it. “I am at a loss for words as how this first play only took one second off the game clock,” NFL analyst Ryan Paganetti posted. Sharp also pointed out that Thursday’s game should’ve went to overtime. He stated the extra four

item.title: Yankees Getting ‘Ultra Aggressive’ in Pursuit of Top FA Reliever
item.description: Adrian Morejon Yankees Getty According to an MLB insider, the New York Yankees are getting “ultra aggressive” in their pursuit of top free-agent reliever Adrian Morejon. The Yankees have already brought back their own free agents, David Bednar and Tim Hill, plus they inked Brent Suter and Jonathan Loaisiga. But New York isn’t stopping there, as they want the biggest fish in the free-agent reliever pond this winter: Morejon. Yankees Badly Want Adrian Morejon Per MLB insider Bob Nightengale, the Yankees are doing everything that they can to sign Morejon, who has pitched the past eight seasons for the San Diego Padres. “The New York Yankees, who have already spent $48.4 million on free agent relievers this winter, have made free-agent lefty Adrian Morejon their No. 1 priority and have become ultra-aggressive in their active pursuit to sign him before the lockout, persons involved with negotiations say,” Nightengale wrote on X . The New York Yankees, who have already spent $48.4 million on free agent relievers this winter, have made free-agent lefty Adrian Morejon their No. 1 priority and have become ultra-aggressive in their active pursuit to sign him before the lockout, persons involved with… — Bob Nightengale (@BNightengale) November 27, 2026 Adrian Morejon Will Get a Huge Contract Based on the going rate for free-agent pitching that we’ve seen so far this offseason, it seems clear that Morejon is going to get a huge contract in free agency. At a minimum, it feels like Morejon is going to get a five-year, $100 million deal, but he may get even more. It’s a lot of money to pay for a relief pitcher, but Morejon is about as elite as it gets from the left side. With so many teams trying to sign him, including the rival Toronto Blue Jays, Yankees GM Brian Cashman clearly feels like this is the guy that he needs to get to transform his bullpen into one of the very best in the entire league. If the Yankees do sign Morejon , he will be leaving the National League for the first time in his MLB career to pitch for an American League team, and he’ll be heading to the pressure cooker that is the AL East, to boot. But Morejon’s stuff is about as elite as it gets in the league from the left-hand side, and if the Yankees sign the fireballer, it makes their bullpen that much more dangerous heading into next season. item.title: Knicks’ Mike Brown toasts Tyler Nickel for ‘physical’ surprise debut vs. Cavs
item.description: Knicks’ Mike Brown toasts Tyler Nickel for ‘physical’ surprise debut vs. Cavs appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . NEW YORK — 2026 Emirates NBA Cup Group Play continued on Wednesday night. New York Knicks head coach Mike Brown treated his team’s game against the Cleveland Cavaliers like a science experiment. In other words, it was business as usual for New York despite the higher stakes. These Knicks simply aren’t as desperate or hungry as they were at this time last year. Their 2025 NBA Emirates Cup victory proved in a small sample size that they were capable of winning at a high level. The ultimate vindication for their players and staff, however, came along with the 2026 NBA Finals Trophy they earned in June. New York is more focused on defending that title than the one they won in Las Vegas. Without organizational pressure to maximize their point differential this time around, Brown turned to the least experienced player on his bench to help give his Knicks an edge. Rookie sharpshooter Tyler Nickel, in his first opportunity at the NBA level, scored five points on 2-3 FG in nine minutes. His coach told reporters at Madison Square Garden that the 23-year-old wasn’t on his minutes sheet going into the game, but delivered exactly what he was looking for when called upon. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “I just thought we needed a lift from some place. I thought if he came in and hit a three, the bench would get into it. It would kind of get everybody hyped. And it could help us with a little bit of a momentum shift, if that could happen. And he did. He did more than that…he was a physical presence. He was just running around and running into people, going at 100 mph, and it was beautiful to see. We needed to shift the momentum in the physicality area. And he brought a lot of that to the table in his 8.5 minutes,” Brown said postgame. Knicks earned these stress-tests of their depth with NBA title win Nickel was certainly not perfect in his first NBA minutes. The rookie was thrown into an important stretch, of an important game, against the same opponent his team bested in last season’s Eastern Conference Finals. He made one of his two attempts from behind the 3-point line, which was good; he also committed four personal fouls, which was not. Brown didn’t mind at all. The coach added after the game that Nickel’s errors were made with — or as the result of playing with — gusto. “He got a layup in transition because he got out and ran. Even some of the fouls, they were just good fouls. Because he was just playing hard. Our guys felt that, responded to it, and liked it. They kind of rallied around it,” Brown told reporters. Nickel seems like a natural fit under the coach who proudly cares about the process that went into decisions more than he does their exact results. item.title: Tinubu, the Igbo and the politics of bread soaked in water, by Emmanuel Aziken
item.description: Four years ago, when Bola Ahmed Tinubu visited Enugu as a presidential candidate, he confronted a crowd that appeared less than enthusiastic about his ambition with a warning that has since acquired an enduring political significance. If they refused to support him and he eventually became president, he suggested, they might have to make do with a slice of bread soaked in water. It may have been intended as political banter, but the message was not lost on the people of the South-East. The symbolism became even more pronounced after his victory when the president-elect constituted his inauguration committee without a single Igbo representative. For many in the region, it was an early indication of the place they might occupy in the new political order. Three and a half years into his presidency, Tinubu’s relationship with the South-East has remained a mixture of gestures of inclusion and lingering questions about the region’s place in his administration. To his credit, he departed from the approach of his predecessor, Muhammadu Buhari, by appointing Igbo into the commanding heights of the military. However, beyond that, questions remain about the administration’s commitment to equitable representation. The South-West presently has 10 ministers and ministers of state in the federal cabinet, compared with four from the South-East, following the exit of former Minister of State for Labour, Nkeiruka Onyejeocha, from Abia State. While constitutional requirements for ministerial representation are being met, the disparity raises legitimate questions about the spirit of federal character and the extent to which every region enjoys a sense of belonging in the federation. Curiously, some supporters of Tinubu in the South-East insist that the region has never had it so good in terms of appointments, access and federal patronage. Their position deserves consideration, but it does not erase the wider perception that the region remains inadequately represented in the distribution of political opportunities. There is also the question of electoral calculation. Before the 2023 election, Tinubu’s political strategy appeared to depend heavily on consolidating support in the South-West and making significant gains in the North. The political landscape has since changed. His administration is facing growing discontent in parts of the North, while the economic consequences of its policies have generated opposition across the country. Against this background, the President’s renewed courtship of the South-East appears to carry greater political significance. His meeting with Igbo residents in Lagos last Monday was particularly revealing. The atmosphere was warm and enthusiastic. Unlike the stern warning of four years ago, Tinubu was relaxed and playful, even reminding his audience of how they had disappointed him in 2023. He was referring to his defeat by Peter Obi in Lagos during the presidential election. Unfortunately, the President and some of his political assoc

item.title: A tale of interlocking blocks, by Muyiwa Adetiba
item.description: The traffic in Victoria Island in the past month had to be experienced to be appreciated. I once spent two hours from Falomo Bridge, Ikoyi to the Mobil petrol station on Victoria Island, a journey that would have been walkable if the weather was kinder and security better. The case of an ‘egbon’ was even worse. He reportedly left Metropolitan Club for his home off Ligali Ayorinde. It is a journey that would take 10 to 15 minutes on a good day. It took him three hours on this fateful evening. It was so bad that this 85year-old man was tempted to walk but for the restraint of his driver and the caution of the friend he was chatting with on the phone. The ostensible reason for the gridlock was the work being done on an Ozumba Mbadiwe stretch which had refused to acknowledge the several palliatives done on it during the rainy season. Lagos State in its wisdom then decided to do something more permanent by using interlocking blocks. Hopefully, the traffic nightmare is over. At least for the time being. The use of interlocking blocks, otherwise called Interlocking Concrete Block Pavements (ICBP) for some roads, seems the way to go. Especially in waterlogged areas with heavy traffic. It is said to be a system where individual blocks which are held together without mortar or adhesives, serve to distribute heavy loads across multiple units. Its strength, like a broom, is in the collective. It is, also like a broom, a pitiable sight when loosened or dislodged. It is even hazardous as loose blocks can cause havoc to motorists. I am no expert, but in my opinion, the blocks are invariably dislodged when the foundation is not tight and firmly compressed before the laying of interlocking blocks with the result that certain areas begin to sink or cave in with time. It could also happen when the edges are not properly fused together with concrete. They are, in other words, as strong as their weakest link. And when this weak link is not quickly remedied, the road begins to disintegrate. This is when a stitch in time would have saved nine. This is when unfortunately, from all I have seen, authorities look the other way. I virtually witnessed the creation and almost the disintegration of a road in Oniru, Victoria Island. Sometimes called the Alternative Road, Akinogun Road was first constructed as a two lane road during the Fashola era to take traffic off Ozumba Mbadiwe by bye-passing the Lekki toll gate. To underscore its importance, the Sanwo-Olu era turned it to four lanes with interlocking blocks. If it was important before, it is now even more so because it is the road that now links commuters in that axis to the Coastal Road. Traffic has understandably, become heavier on the road. And probably because of this, especially during peak periods, another U-turn was very recently created that was probably not in the original design. This U-turn makes access to the Coastal Road easier and faster. It is unfortunately from the creation of this U-turn that the disintegr

item.title: 2027: Tinubu failed to fulfil his promises, he must go – Obi
item.description: By Ugochukwu Alaribe UMUAHIA — Presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Mr Peter Obi, has said President Bola Tinubu must be voted out in the 2027 presidential election for Nigeria to experience the change and development it desires. Obi, who spoke on Friday at the Primetime Event Centre, along the Port Harcourt-Aba Expressway, Aba, Abia State, accused the Tinubu administration of failing to fulfil its campaign promises and worsening poverty in the country. He assured residents that the government he and his running mate, Senator Rabiu Kwankwaso, were seeking to form would unite the country and transform its economic and social sectors. The former Anambra State governor said the presidency required energy and commitment, arguing that it should not be treated as a retirement home. “Tinubu has failed to fulfil all his promises, including the restoration of the power sector. We will generate, transmit and distribute at least 10,000MW. Any money we borrow must be for investment. “The presidency requires energy; it is not a retirement home. We are tired of Tinubu’s government. Tinubu must go for a better Nigeria to emerge,” he said. Obi said his proposed administration would prioritise national unity, recalling that Nigeria had previously enjoyed stronger bonds across its different regions. “Let me assure you that the government Kwankwaso and I are seeking to form will unite Nigeria. Yesterday, I was in Minna, and I told them that Nigeria used to be united. No wonder Nnamdi Azikiwe and Chukwuemeka Ojukwu were born in Zungeru. We are going to reunite Nigeria. “The Nigeria we want is one where a child of nobody can become somebody,” he said. He also criticised the Federal Government’s borrowing, alleging that the Tinubu administration had borrowed more than previous administrations combined without commensurate visible results. According to him, his proposed government would focus on production, job creation and economic prosperity rather than continued dependence on consumption. “Kwankwaso and I want to form a government that will not give you excuses. We are going to form a government that will bring prosperity and production back to Nigeria. We will remove this country from consumption to production. “We already know the excuses, and we will tackle the challenges. Our government will demonstrate compassion, commitment and the zeal to get the job done,” he said. On corruption, Obi pledged that his administration would ensure public funds were deployed for the benefit of Nigerians. He questioned the utilisation of government loans, contrasting current borrowing with previous investments in major infrastructure projects such as the Kainji Dam. Obi further claimed that the number of Nigerians living in poverty had increased from 87 million when Tinubu assumed office to more than 140 million. He also expressed concern over youth unemployment, promising increased investment in education and healthcare if elected. Turning to the econ

item.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi The Chairman of Agatu Local Government Area of Benue State, Mr Melvin Ejeh, has vowed to ensure the arrest and prosecution of those responsible for the killing of an officer of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), Inspector Anyebe Anya. Anya was reportedly killed by armed men who attacked him at his duty post at a checkpoint in Agatu a few days ago. The assailants were also said to have carted away his service rifle after the attack. Ejeh gave the assurance when he visited the deceased officer’s family in Otukpo to commiserate with them, describing Anya as a hardworking, honest and dedicated officer. He vowed that those behind the killing would not escape justice, assuring the bereaved family that efforts were already underway to track down and apprehend the perpetrators. “Those that killed him will not go unpunished. We will get all of them. I knew him personally. He was a very hardworking, honest man who was committed to his work. “The whole community is mourning his death. The people of Agatu are shocked and grieving over his death. “We console his family. He was a committed officer. I can assure you that we will get those involved and they will be brought to justice. There is a hunt for them already. “The entire Agatu people will not rest until he gets justice, that I can assure his family,” the chairman said. Efforts to reach the Public Relations Officer of the Benue State NSCDC Command, SC Michael Ejelikwu, for comments were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report. The post Manhunt launched for killers of NSCDC officer in Benue appeared first on Vanguard News .
